places.name: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum
places.connection: Primary visual reference for bathhouse architecture - confirmed by Miyazaki

places.name: Ghibli Museum
places.connection: Official museum with Spirited Away production materials

places.name: Kodak Theatre (now Dolby Theatre)
places.connection: Venue where Spirited Away won the Academy Award for Best Animated Feature on March 23, 2003.

places.name: Jiufen Old Street
places.connection: This hillside town with its narrow alleys and red lanterns is famously believed to be an inspiration. However, Miyazaki has personally denied visiting or using it as a model.

places.name: Nikkō Tōshō-gū Shrine
places.connection: The ornate, colorful, and intricate carvings of mythical creatures at this UNESCO World Heritage site are reflected in the lavish decorations of the spirit world.

places.name: Venice Film Festival (Palazzo del Cinema)
places.connection: Location of the film's international premiere on September 7, 2001.

places.name: Studio Ghibli
places.connection: The animation studio where the film was conceived, written, and produced.

places.name: Edo-Tokyo Open Air Architectural Museum
places.connection: Miyazaki confirmed this museum, which preserves historic Japanese buildings, was a primary visual inspiration for the spirit world's architecture, especially the bathhouse.

places.name: Dōgo Onsen Honkan
places.connection: This historic public bathhouse is widely cited as a direct architectural inspiration for Yubaba's bathhouse.

places.name: Shima Onsen, Sekizenkan Ryokan
places.connection: The red bridge leading to this traditional inn is said to be the model for the bridge Chihiro must cross to enter the spirit world.

places.name: Kanaguya History Museum (Shibu Onsen)
places.connection: A multi-story, labyrinthine wooden inn whose complex exterior is another strong visual precedent for the Aburaya bathhouse.

places.name: Notoyaryokan
places.connection: A historic inn in the Ginzan Onsen area, its traditional architecture and riverside setting contribute to the film's overall aesthetic.

places.name: Ginzan Onsen
places.connection: Taisho-era hot spring town - closest real-world equivalent to spirit world atmosphere

places.name: Jiufen Old Street
places.connection: Disputed but visually striking - Miyazaki denied, but fans embrace connection

places.name: Dogo Onsen
places.connection: Likely inspiration for bathhouse architecture (3,000-year-old onsen)
